litematica_container_filler.config.comme: Enable or disable the core features of the Container Filler.

When enabled, the mod continuously scans and fills reachable containers within the area fill radius. The hotkey can be configured on the same row. The manual fill hotkey still only handles the container you are looking at.
When enabled, the mod will automatically scan for and fill missing containers.

OFF: Only fill the container you are currently looking at.
ON: Automatically scan all containers within the specified radius.
Fill radius for Area Fill Mode (0 - 1024 blocks, 0 means unlimited).
Render radius for missing container highlights (0 - 1024 blocks).
When enabled, highlights and filling actions will only apply to containers within the current Litematica render layer.
When enabled, automatically hides the highlight box when the container perfectly matches the schematic.
Receive Servux data to view container contents through walls without opening them.
Highlights missing, incorrect, or unsynced schematic containers in the world with wireframes.
When enabled, container highlights render through terrain and blocks (X-Ray).
When enabled, containers that are empty in the schematic but contain items in the real world will be highlighted as overfilled/excess.
Delay between automated fill actions (in Ticks). Higher is slower.

When enabled, the mod will treat two bottom-connected barrels as a single large double barrel (requires Carpet mod's 'largeBarrels' rule on the server).
If your server does not have large barrels enabled, keep this OFF to prevent barrel slot offset issues.

Replace required materials in the schematic with another item.
Format: source_id->target_id (e.g. minecraft:stone->minecraft:cobblestone).
Use minecraft:air as the target to ignore that material and skip filling it.
Supports custom names using # (e.g. minecraft:stone#filler1->minecraft:dirt#filler2).
The replaced item will be stripped of NBT/enchantments to ensure matching.
Multiple rules can be added.
Automatically open Shulker Boxes in your inventory to extract required items when materials run out.

Invoke: use QuickShulker's open packet and requires QuickShulker to be installed.
Simulate Click: simulate a right click on the shulker slot in the player inventory, for other quick-shulker-like mods that listen to GUI right clicks.
When enabled, automatically stashes unrelated items into a Shulker Box if your inventory is full to free up space.

Projection filling frees inventory space with a speed-first ordered strategy.
Items taken from shulker boxes are put back into their source or matching shulker boxes first. If none are available, unrelated items not needed by the current task are stashed into the first suitable shulker box.
When enabled, incorrect or excess items will be dropped on the ground instead of being returned to your inventory.
When enabled and you have server OP permissions, the mod will actively request data for unopened containers from the server.

Disabling this will make the machine ignore all safety delays and fill at maximum speed (may cause bugs or result in a server kick).
Use with caution.
When enabled, the fill work state is automatically turned off when leaving the world, switching worlds or dimensions, changing player session, or dying/respawning.
Compatibility mode for plugin servers and anti-cheat environments. When enabled, automated container click packets are queued and sent slowly. Keep this off on normal servers.
Maximum automated container click packets sent per game tick when Slow Click Packets is enabled.

Controls support for Carpet's largeBarrels rule.
Off: always treat barrels as normal single barrels.
On: always merge two back-to-back barrels into one large barrel.
Auto: only merges back-to-back barrel pairs after known real slot count confirms 54-slot large-barrel behavior; unknown slot count stays as normal barrels to avoid false highlights. Empty unopened large barrels may need manual On until real data is synced.
Choose whether the container filter list is disabled, used as a whitelist, or used as a blacklist.

Container block IDs used by the whitelist/blacklist. Supports * wildcards, for example minecraft:*_shulker_box. Non-vanilla containers can be added manually by block ID; the mod also tries to recognize common inventory block entities automatically.
When enabled, required items will be printed from thin air in Creative mode, ignoring inventory limitations.
Legacy hide UI option, kept only for migrating old config files.
Hide automatically opened container screens during projection fill work.
When enabled, if a schematic container is empty but the real container contains items, filling may throw those real items out. Warning: this can drop valuable items on the ground.

Enables the selected container tool.
Switch Container Tool: cycles the selected mode.
Execute Container Tool: runs it on the looked-at container.
Close All Tool Modes: disables tools and fill work.

Selected tool for the unified container tool hotkey.
Clear: empties the looked-at container.
Fill Full: fills it from inventory with one unambiguous item type.
Sync: first reads a template container, then copies that layout into same-type target containers.
Container Packing: moves the looked-at container contents into inventory shulker boxes, preferring boxes already holding the same item, then any box with free space.
Container Packing is skipped when no quick-shulker support is available.

When enabled, the Sync Container tool may open quick shulker boxes or use TakeItOut to fetch missing template items.
When disabled, Sync Container only uses items already in the player inventory.
Hide automatically opened container screens while container tools are running.

Toggle the clear container tool.
Use the clear trigger hotkey to process only the container you are looking at.

Toggle the fill-full tool.
Use the fill-full trigger hotkey to process only the container you are looking at.

Toggle the sync container tool.
First trigger reads the looked-at container as a template.
Later triggers sync the looked-at container.
Render containers that are empty but need items.
Render containers that contain some required items but are not complete.
Render containers with extra items or excessive item counts.
Render containers that contain wrong item types.
Render containers that already match the schematic.
Render containers whose real inventory data has not been synchronized yet.
Render schematic containers that do not currently have a matching placed container block in the real world.
Render the translucent full-block highlight body.
Render the small top plate that makes highlighted containers easier to identify.
Render a flat animated marker above the container currently being filled.
Render animated waiting markers above queued containers.
Render markers above containers skipped because required materials are missing.
Maximum number of queued-container markers to render at once. Lower values improve FPS in large container piles.
How long a transient task marker remains after a fill operation finishes.
Opacity multiplier for the translucent highlight body.
Size of the top highlight plate.
Scale of animated task markers.
Color when the container is completely empty but the schematic requires items. Default: Blue. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the container has required items but not enough, or in the wrong slots. Default: Yellow. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the items and slots are correct, but the amount exceeds the requirement, or there are extra items. Default: Pink. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the container holds completely wrong items compared to the schematic. Default: Red. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the container perfectly matches the schematic. Default: Green. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the real container data has not yet been fetched from the server. Default: Orange. Use hex ARGB format.
Color when the schematic has a container but the real world has no placed container there. Default: Slate. Use hex ARGB format.
Color for the animated marker above the container currently being filled. Use hex ARGB format.
Color for queued-container waiting markers. Use hex ARGB format.
Color for containers skipped because materials are missing. Use hex ARGB format.

Fixed Card: a clean information card stays in a stable screen position without anchor lines.
Anchored Card: the older style that points from the selected container to the HUD card.
Controls the transparency of the container tool HUD panel.
Controls how smoothly the tool HUD animation updates. Lower values feel softer but slower.

Fixed Card: horizontal distance from the screen center.
Anchored Card: screen-space distance between the selected container marker and the tool HUD panel.
Scales the tool HUD card, including its panel and icons. 100 is the default size.
Scales only the animated icon inside the tool HUD card. 100 matches the card scale.
Horizontal HUD card offset relative to the screen crosshair. You can drag the HUD card in the render editor.
Vertical HUD card offset relative to the screen crosshair. You can drag the HUD card in the render editor.
Maximum update rate for tool HUD layout and animation. 0 means unlimited.

Read or sync the looked-at container.

Quickly switch between 'Single Gaze Mode' and 'Area Scan Mode'.
Hotkey to open this mod's configuration menu (Default: L + C).

litematica_container_filler.config.comme:
When enabled, shows the selected container tool and action hint
near the crosshair while looking at a container.

Controls where items go when the Clear Container tool removes them.
Drop: throws them onto the ground.
Inventory: quick-moves them into your inventory and aborts if there is not enough space.

Controls which features use the container filter.
Projection Fill: schematic filling, area fill, manual schematic fill, and container highlights.
Container Tools: clear, fill-full, sync, and packing tools.
Both: applies the same filter everywhere.
Maximum animation rebuild rate for filling, queued, and missing-material markers. 0 means unlimited.
